big_idea: CONGRUENT means SAME SIZE and SAME SHAPE. We match faces, lengths, and angles.
learning_intention: We are learning to identify congruent faces, lengths, and angles.
student_learning_goal: I can identify congruent faces, lengths, and angles.
success_criteria: I can SAY what congruent means.
I can DECIDE if 2 objects are congruent.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Trekker Tig and Compass Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Anchor chart 'Congruent = Same Size + Same Shape'
Congruent Face Match Cards (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Compass Coco: I have 2 face cards. Are they CONGRUENT? Same size AND same shape? Tig opens: 'SAME SHAPE, SAME SIZE — that's CONGRUENT!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Compass Coco the Cat puppet with compass. 'Geometers — today we learn CONGRUENT.'

Define. 'CONGRUENT = SAME SIZE and SAME SHAPE. Both must match!'

Demo. Show 2 squares of the SAME SIZE. 'Same shape (square)? Yes. Same size? Yes. CONGRUENT!'

Show a square + a rectangle. 'Same shape? NO — square vs rectangle. NOT congruent.'

Show 2 squares of DIFFERENT SIZES. 'Same shape? Yes. Same size? NO. NOT congruent.'

'Compass Coco says — BOTH must match!'

Show how to TEST. 'I overlap them. If they match exactly, congruent!'

Now try with 3D faces. 'A cube has 6 faces — all congruent squares!'

'A rectangular prism has 6 faces — but only OPPOSITE faces are congruent.'

Lengths and angles too. 'All edges of a cube are CONGRUENT (same length). All angles are right angles (also congruent).'

Now each pair gets the Congruent Face Match Cards (20 cards in 10 congruent pairs). They:
1. Spread cards out.
2. Find 5 congruent pairs.
3. Identify 2 NON-congruent pairs.

'Compass Coco says — match by overlapping or measuring!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Match Card Sets. Pairs find 5 congruent pairs.
Identify 2 NON-congruent pairs (close but not match).
Stretch: explain 1 reason a pair is NOT congruent.

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Hold cards up to compare visually. NO-MATERIALS PATH: children use their own two hands as shape testers (fingers spread = pentagon, fist = square). Compare hand shapes for congruence.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: defines; matches; tests; explains; consistency.

discussion_prompts: Find 2 congruent faces in our classroom.
consolidation.exit_routine: Tig's congruent refrain — 'SAME SHAPE, SAME SIZE — that's CONGRUENT!' (3x). Each child tests one face pair with overlay.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says CONGRUENT for SAME SHAPE only — repairing the size-blind trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On congruent faces, the trap is van Hiele Level 1 visual judgment: child says 'same' if it LOOKS same, ignoring size. Battista (2007) frames this as the L1→L2 transition.

Yesterday Lesson 2 built structures. Today we test FACE CONGRUENCE. Lesson 4 map+move; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Match activity. Child says 2 squares (small + big) are congruent.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Compass Coco asks — same SHAPE? Same SIZE?'

Probe. 'Both squares — same shape? Yes. Same size? NO — one is bigger.'

Generalise. 'Compass Coco says — CONGRUENT means BOTH size AND shape. Either one missing = NOT congruent.'

If still confused: overlap. 'Lay small on big. They don't match — NOT congruent.'
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child can name 'same shape' but freezes on size: drop to a SAME shape, DIFFERENT size pair; child names 'NOT congruent because sizes differ'.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child accepts congruent but rejects rotation: physically rotate; child sees rotation doesn't change congruence.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child tests but cannot articulate: force 'these faces ARE/ARE NOT congruent because ___'.

parts_outline.task: Decide YES/NO if 4 pairs are congruent.
Explain WHY one pair is NOT congruent.
